title: Interleaved Hotkey & Coldpath Benchmark to Map Hit-Rate Knee for Prefix KV Cache
creator: Maya Patel
description: Objective: Build a repeatable, parameterized benchmark that exercises interleaved hotkey and coldpath access patterns against the prefix KV cache to identify the 'knee' in hit-rate vs memory tradeoff and detect small regressions in token p95 and throughput. Motivations: existing single-pattern harnesses (hotset-only or uniform) miss interference effects when multiple tenant-like workloads are multiplexed. This experiment targets real-world mixes (chat + search + rerank) with different prefix lengths and sequence-length distributions to reveal non-linear latency cliffs. The harness should produce deterministic traces, per-token latency histograms, and a regression signal that can be fed into our CI gate.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook and config templates checked into runtime/benchmarks/kv-interleaved
Benchmark can be reproduced locally and on perf-cluster via make bench:interleaved
Metrics emitted to grafana-prod (tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 token latency, KV hit-rate, RSS/alloc, eviction rate)
Automated regression detector (baseline vs experiment) flags >3% p95 increase or >5% tokens/sec drop
Documentation: confluence page with experiment design and interpretation guidelines
steps: Design workload mixes: chat-heavy (70% short seq), search-heavy (40% long seq), and mixed-tempo (50/30/20) with hotkey skews 10:1, 50:1, 200:1
Implement generator that emits interleaved request streams with configurable prefix-lengths and token budgets
Instrument runtime to tag requests with workload-id and prefix-hash for per-workload KPIs
Run parameter sweep over cache sizes (4GB, 8GB, 16GB, 32GB), slab configurations, and prefetch window (0, 4, 16 prefixes)
Capture full traces (KV access patterns + kernel timelines) and store artifacts under s3://redwood-perf/kv_interleaved/
Implement regression check in perf CI (compare new run to baseline with bootstrap confidence intervals)
observations: Preliminary run (4GB cache) shows a sharp p95 cliff when hotkey skew exceeds ~80:1 for mixed workloads — p95 increases 38% while hit-rate drops 12%
Increasing prefetch window to 16 reduced cold_miss_latency by ~30% on search-heavy mixes but increased memory pressure and eviction churn
Multi-tenant mixes amplify tail effects compared to isolated hotset runs; single-tenant baselines understate p95 regressions
Noise floor for tokens/sec measurement on perf-cluster is ~1.5% — regression detector will use bootstrap sampling to avoid false positives
notes_and_tradeoffs: We will prioritize determinism for CI by fixing random seeds and synthetic key namespaces; this reduces realism but improves regression signal fidelity
Running full parameter sweeps is expensive — adopt staged approach: quick smoke sweep (3 sizes) then targeted deep runs for promising configurations
Prefetch reduces cold-path latency but may create eviction storms; consider adaptive prefetch tied to observed access locality
Deciding an alert threshold balances noise vs sensitivity; initial thresholds set conservatively and will be tuned after 3 weeks of runs
